heading: Web Push subscriptions
body:
Web Push lets the server tell the user about something new while the page is closed. Grant `push` in `tac.browserApis`. A Go service adds a `// @Needs` field `push Push`; JavaScript and TypeScript use `@Needs push`.

| Call (Go name) | Needs a click or key handler | The answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Supported()` | No | `true` or `false` at once |
| `Subscribe(applicationServerKey)` | Yes | `PushSubscribed { endpoint, p256dh, auth, expirationTime }` |
| `Subscription()` | No | `PushSubscribed`, or `PushUnsubscribed` with an empty `endpoint` |
| `Unsubscribe()` | No | `PushUnsubscribed { endpoint }` |

`Subscribe` takes the server's VAPID public key as base64url: 65 bytes that start with `0x04`. It asks for notification permission first. Send the fields of `PushSubscribed` to your Yon server, for example with an `@HTTPClient`; the server encrypts each message (RFC 8291) and sends it to `endpoint`. Tachyon does not send push messages. When the user says no, the service gets `BrowserCallFailed` with `api` `push`.

A build that grants `push` ships a second service worker, `/.tachyon/tac-push-sw.js`, with the scope `/.tachyon/push/`. It never caches pages. It shows each message as a notification. Send the message as JSON: `{"title": "New mail", "body": "From Ana", "path": "/mail/7", "tag": "mail-7"}`. Plain text becomes the body, and the host name is the title when none is given. A click on the notification focuses a window that is already on `path`, or opens it. Only a path on the same origin is opened; any other value opens `/`.

Web Push needs HTTPS or `localhost`. On iPhone and iPad, Safari gives Web Push only to an app added to the Home Screen, from iOS 16.4. A native app (macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android) has no Web Push: `Supported()` answers `false`, and the other calls fail with "Web Push needs a web browser. The native app has no Push API." Native push (APNs, FCM) is not part of Tachyon yet.

Only Go, JavaScript and TypeScript services have `Push` today. Rust, Swift, Java, Kotlin, C#, F#, Dart, Ruby, Lua and C++ services have no `Push` type yet, so those tabs are missing, and Python has no browser APIs.
